sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Yorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-约尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 Dealbook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场，采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mamdani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·马姆达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews at nytimes.com and in the Times app on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我们将在 nytimes.com 和《纽约时报》App 上对部分采访进行直播。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, love it or hate it, over the past seven years, the Affordable Care Act has woven its way into American lives.
sentences.zh: 今天，无论你喜欢还是讨厌，在过去的七年里，《平价医疗法案》已经融入了美国人的生活。

sentences.en: As the Republican health care bill moves rapidly through Congress, what the repeal of Obamacare might mean for a rural community in West Virginia.
sentences.zh: 随着共和党医疗法案在国会快速推进，废除奥巴马医改对西弗吉尼亚州的一个农村社区意味着什么。

sentences.en: And, from Solange to Rufus Wainwright, what music can tell us about this moment in time.
sentences.zh: 此外，从索兰热到鲁福斯·温赖特，音乐能告诉我们关于这个时代怎样的信息。

sentences.en: It's Friday, March 10th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 3 月 10 日，星期五。

sentences.en: Good morning, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: I've got a few things I'd like to say.
sentences.zh: 我有几句话想说。

sentences.en: First of all, I would like to walk you through exactly what the American Health Care Act is and how important it is to repeal and replace Obamacare,
sentences.zh: 首先，我想向大家详细介绍什么是《美国医疗法案》，以及废除并替代奥巴马医改是多么重要，

sentences.en: not just because the law is collapsing, but because the law is going to get even worse if we do nothing.
sentences.zh: 不仅是因为这项法律正在崩溃，还因为如果我们什么都不做，它会变得更糟糕。

sentences.en: With his shirt sleeves rolled up and a remote control in his hand.
sentences.zh: 他挽起衬衫袖子，手里拿着一个遥控器。

sentences.en: Let me show you what our problem is and what we're trying to do.
sentences.zh: 让我向你们展示我们的问题所在以及我们正在努力做的事情。

sentences.en: The Speaker of the House, Paul Ryan, walked Americans through a PowerPoint presentation on Thursday morning.
sentences.zh: 周四上午，众议院议长保罗·瑞安向美国人展示了一份 PPT 演示文稿。

sentences.en: So we have a three-pronged approach, a three-pronged approach to repealing and replacing Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有一个三管齐下的方法，即废除和替代奥巴马医改的三管齐下之策。

sentences.en: Ryan laid out Republican criticism of the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 瑞安阐述了共和党对《平价医疗法案》的批评。

sentences.en: Take a look at what's going on around the country.
sentences.zh: 看看全国各地正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: This just shows you a map of the premium increases just this year alone.
sentences.zh: 这只是一张展示今年保费上涨情况的地图。

sentences.en: Minnesota, 59% increase in their health insurance premiuMs.
sentences.zh: 明尼苏达州，医疗保险保费上涨了 59%。

sentences.en: Pennsylvania, 53% increase in their health insurance premiuMs.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州，医疗保险保费上涨了 53%。

sentences.en: And how their new plan would fix it with tax incentives, health savings accounts, and more choices.
sentences.zh: 以及他们的新计划将如何通过税收优惠、健康储蓄账户和更多选择来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: These are long-standing conservative principles that those of us who've been working in health care for about 20 years have been fighting for, dreaming about, working toward.
sentences.zh: 这些都是长期的保守派原则，我们这些从事医疗保健工作大约 20 年的人一直在为之奋斗、梦想和努力。

sentences.en: Now we have an opportunity to do that.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有机会做到这一点了。

sentences.en: Later in the day, the Republican plan passed the second of two House committees.
sentences.zh: 当天晚些时候，共和党计划通过了众议院两个委员会中的第二个。

sentences.en: That now brings it before a full vote in the House.
sentences.zh: 这使其现在提交给众议院全体表决。

sentences.en: At the same time, opposition to the bill is growing.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，对该法案的反对声音也在不断增加。

sentences.en: Liberals are against it because they like Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 自由派反对它，因为他们喜欢奥巴马医改。

sentences.en: Conservatives who oppose it say it's too much like Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 反对它的保守派则表示它太像奥巴马医改了。

sentences.en: And many doctors, regardless of their politics, simply fear for the health of their most vulnerable patients.
sentences.zh: 许多医生，无论其政治立场如何，单纯在为他们最脆弱的病人的健康感到担忧。

sentences.en: Dr. Jakes?
sentences.zh: 杰克斯医生？

sentences.en: Yes, this is he.
sentences.zh: 对，我就是。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Michael Barbaro from The Times.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: We called up Dr. Mitch Jakes, who works at a clinic in rural West Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我们打电话给米奇·杰克斯医生，他在西弗吉尼亚州乡村的一家诊所工作。

sentences.en: Good afternoon.
sentences.zh: 下午好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: Sounds like it's been a busy day.
sentences.zh: 听起来今天是很忙的一天。

sentences.en: What happened so far?
sentences.zh: 到目前为止发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's a typical condition.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一种典型的情况。

sentences.en: From that, I had another patient who, we saw about 13 or 14 patients.
sentences.zh: 由此，我还有另一个病人，我们大约看了 13 或 14 个病人。

sentences.en: Everybody do okay?
sentences.zh: 大家都还好吗？

sentences.en: Everybody's doing fine.
sentences.zh: 大家都很好。

sentences.en: Is that pretty typical?
sentences.zh: 这相当典型吗？

sentences.en: That's an average morning.
sentences.zh: 这是一个普通的早晨。

sentences.en: So that's typical for the patients we care for and pretty typical for rural West Virginia.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我们照顾的病人来说很典型，对西弗吉尼亚州乡村来说也相当典型。

sentences.en: So tell me about this community where you're a doctor now.
sentences.zh: 那么跟我讲讲你现在担任医生的这个社区吧。

sentences.en: We're working at the clinic I'm working at was originally United Mine Workers Clinic.
sentences.zh: 我们工作的诊所最初是联合矿工诊所。

sentences.en: It was started in the late 60s, early 70s.
sentences.zh: 它始于 60 年代末、70 年代初。

sentences.en: And it is an area of southern West Virginia where there was at one time still active mines.
sentences.zh: 它是西弗吉尼亚州南部的一个地区，那里曾经还有活跃的煤矿。

sentences.en: Coal mining has been part of the culture in this part of the world forever.
sentences.zh: 煤炭开采一直是世界这一地区文化的一部分。

sentences.en: Almost every family we see has someone who either was a coal miner and got laid off or family members were in the coal industry.
sentences.zh: 我们看诊的几乎每个家庭都有人曾是煤矿工人并被解雇，或者家庭成员在煤炭行业工作。

sentences.en: It's the major employer of good jobs in this region, or it was until recently.
sentences.zh: 它是这个地区提供好工作的最主要雇主，直到最近还是如此。

sentences.en: It sounds like this is a poor community.
sentences.zh: 听起来这是一个贫困社区。

sentences.en: How much is what you're seeing about the interaction of poverty and health?
sentences.zh: 你所看到的现象中，贫困与健康的相互影响占了多大比重？

sentences.en: If you look at the states, West Virginia and Mississippi, traditionally the lowest income in the United States.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看各州，西弗吉尼亚州和密西西比州传统上是美国收入最低的。

sentences.en: And I would say with the decline of the coal industry in the last five years, when you get outside the cities in West Virginia,
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，随着过去五年煤炭行业的衰退，当你走到西弗吉尼亚州的城市之外时，

sentences.en: so much of what we're seeing is a result of access where very few people could get health care who didn't have good incomes.
sentences.zh: 我们所看到的大量情况都是由于医疗资源的获取问题造成的，很少有收入不高的人能够获得医疗服务。

sentences.en: It's a combination of things, but certainly poverty plays a part.
sentences.zh: 这是多种因素结合的结果，但贫困无疑占了一部分原因。

sentences.en: So let's talk about before the Affordable Care Act was enacted, was this community getting the health care that it needed?
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈《平价医疗法案》颁布之前，这个社区是否得到了它需要的医疗保健？

sentences.en: For 25 years.
sentences.zh: 持续了 25 年。

sentences.en: And prior to the Affordable Care Act, the only access for people who did not have insurance, and there are many in this,
sentences.zh: 而在《平价医疗法案》颁布之前，没有保险的人唯一的就医途径——这里有很多人——

sentences.en: you could go to the emergency room, you could go to the university, or you could go to a community health center.
sentences.zh: 你可以去急诊室，可以去大学医院，或者可以去社区卫生中心。

sentences.en: I mean, it was not uncommon for someone to go to the emergency room and have a major heart procedure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有人去急诊室做重大心脏手术并不罕见。

sentences.en: Because they didn't have insurance?
sentences.zh: 因为他们没有保险？

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And a year and a half later, they would come and see me with nothing having been done.
sentences.zh: 一年半后，他们来看我时，什么都没做过。

sentences.en: They had not been checked.
sentences.zh: 他们没有接受过检查。

sentences.en: Their blood pressure had not been checked.
sentences.zh: 他们的血压没有检查过。

sentences.en: That was pretty good insurance.
sentences.zh: 那是相当不错的保险。

sentences.en: They couldn't afford a mammogram.
sentences.zh: 他们买不起乳房 X 光检查。

sentences.en: Because of lung disease, they had to pay cash for that.
sentences.zh: 由于肺部疾病，他们不得不为此支付现金。

sentences.en: You know, you tell someone a sleep study would cost $2,000 and a portion of that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你告诉某人睡眠研究要花 2000 美元以及其中的一部分。

sentences.en: So I want to talk to you about the politics of that moment just before the Affordable Care Act gets passed.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在想和你谈谈《平价医疗法案》通过前夕的政治形势。

sentences.en: Because your community, as you're describing it, is not getting the proper health care, the health care that it needs.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所描述的，你的社区没有得到适当的医疗保健，没有得到它需要的医疗保健。

sentences.en: And a lot of the people you're talking about, it sounds like, couldn't afford the insurance.
sentences.zh: 听起来你谈论的很多人都买不起保险。

sentences.en: And then comes President Obama promising a national health care program.
sentences.zh: 然后奥巴马总统承诺推行全国医疗保健计划。

sentences.en: Did the community like the plan he was offering?
sentences.zh: 社区喜欢他提供的这个计划吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's the Affordable Care Act, but not in favor of Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是平价医疗法案，但并不赞成奥巴马医改。

sentences.en: I laugh because I have a number of patients who would come in.
sentences.zh: 我笑是因为我有好几个会来看诊的病人。

sentences.en: I mean, we had an outpouring of patients when the Affordable Care Act was passed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当《平价医疗法案》通过时，我们迎来了病人的爆发。

sentences.en: And they were, it was wonderful for them.
sentences.zh: 而且他们，这对他们来说太棒了。

sentences.en: The word Obamacare is a care system.
sentences.zh: “奥巴马医改”这个词是一个医疗系统。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So I have a number of patients who would say, yeah, I'm glad to get insurance.
sentences.zh: 所以我有很多病人会说，是的，我很高兴能有保险。

sentences.en: I love you.
sentences.zh: 我爱你。

sentences.en: I'm glad we're getting care.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我们得到了照顾。

sentences.en: But that Obamacare stuff, I just don't care for.
sentences.zh: 但那些奥巴马医改的东西，我就是不感兴趣。

sentences.en: I think they've heard Obamacare disparage so much that they don't relate the two.
sentences.zh: 我想他们听到了太多对奥巴马医改的诋毁，以至于他们不把这两者联系起来。

sentences.en: Just to be really clear, the folks you're talking about liked the health care that they were now getting under Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 为了非常明确起见，你所谈论的人们喜欢他们现在通过奥巴马医改获得的医疗保健。

sentences.en: They just didn't like the idea of Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 他们只是不喜欢奥巴马医改这个概念。

sentences.en: I think in general, if you ask someone in West Virginia if they like Obamacare, they're just going to be no.
sentences.zh: 我认为总的来说，如果你问西弗吉尼亚州的人是否喜欢奥巴马医改，他们的回答只会是否定的。

sentences.en: Because there's been so much adverse publicity for the word Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 因为“奥巴马医改”这个词有太多负面宣传。

sentences.en: If they waited an extra hour at the ER, if anything happened, that was due to what is perceived as Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在急诊室多等了一个小时，如果发生了任何事情，那都被归咎于人们所认为的奥巴马医改。

sentences.en: So now several years into Obamacare, what's different for your patients?
sentences.zh: 那么在奥巴马医改实施几年后的今天，你的病人们有什么不同？

sentences.en: What are you seeing day in, day out?
sentences.zh: 你日复一日看到了什么？

sentences.en: I think we're seeing less new patients that have out-of-control diabetes or out-of-control hypertension.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们看到患有失控糖尿病或失控高血压的新病人变少了。

sentences.en: People who go to the hospital come to us for follow-up.
sentences.zh: 去过医院的人会来找我们进行后续随访。

sentences.en: I think, you know, much of care in 2017 is preventative care.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，2017 年的大部分医疗都是预防性医疗。

sentences.en: Make sure people are getting their mammogram.
sentences.zh: 确保人们进行了乳房 X 光检查。

sentences.en: So I think we're doing that much, much, much more routinely.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们更经常、更大量地在做这件事。

sentences.en: And I think it's easier to get people into specialists.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为让人去看专科医生更容易了。

sentences.en: There's still some specialties it's hard to get people to see on Medicaid.
sentences.zh: 仍然有一些专科很难让医疗白卡（Medicaid）患者去看病。

sentences.en: But by and large, we're able to get people to specialists who need to see specialists.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，我们能够让需要看专科医生的患者去看专科医生。

sentences.en: That's the way it should be.
sentences.zh: 这才是它应有的样子。

sentences.en: So I want to know what didn't work about Obamacare for your community.
sentences.zh: 所以我想知道奥巴马医改对你们社区来说有什么行不通的地方。

sentences.en: I think the only thing that didn't work was the initial confusion in the first year trying to get people registered.
sentences.zh: 我认为唯一行不通的就是第一年在试图让人们注册时的最初混乱。

sentences.en: It's a very difficult process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常艰难的过程。

sentences.en: I think for many people, the co-pays, even though they're somewhat subsidized,
sentences.zh: 我认为对许多人来说，共付额即使在某种程度上得到了补贴，

sentences.en: their incomes are so low that there are many patients that I have that simply can't afford the who are working but have very limited incomes.
sentences.zh: 他们的收入也太低了，以至于我有许多病人虽然在工作但收入非常有限，根本负担不起。

sentences.en: And I think many of the insurance policies that are out there have large deductibles.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为现有的许多保险单都有很高的免赔额。

sentences.en: So they might have a $3,000 or $4,000 or $5,000 deductible.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能面临 3000、4000 或 5000 美元的免赔额。

sentences.en: That's high.
sentences.zh: 这太高了。

sentences.en: So the people who have purchased insurance through Obamacare, they're in the same situation as the people who didn't have insurance.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过奥巴马医改购买保险的人，其处境和没有保险的人是一样的。

sentences.en: If you need to get a sleep study or a CAT scan, there's such a large deductible, they will not get those studies.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要做睡眠研究或 CT 扫描，由于免赔额如此之高，他们将不会去做这些检查。

sentences.en: Buy their kid's shoes before they're going to get their study.
sentences.zh: 给孩子买鞋子会排在做检查之前。

sentences.en: So I'm really struck by this.
sentences.zh: 所以我对此深感震撼。

sentences.en: This is a community that clearly benefits from the Affordable Care Act, and yet it voted for a candidate who wants to repeal the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 这是一个明显受益于《平价医疗法案》的社区，然而它却投票给了一个想要废除《平价医疗法案》的候选人。

sentences.en: Well, but the candidate, I think people believe that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是那个候选人，我想人们相信了这一点。

sentences.en: I don't think, or I hope he does.
sentences.zh: 我不认为，或者我希望他是认真的。

sentences.en: I think the problem is that these words get thrown around, and health care was not the only issue.
sentences.zh: 我认为问题在于这些词被到处滥用，而且医疗保健并不是唯一的问题。

sentences.en: Cole was the issue.
sentences.zh: 煤炭才是问题所在。

sentences.en: They voted for a candidate who said he'd bring Cole back, and that's important in this state.
sentences.zh: 他们投票给了一个承诺让煤炭回归的候选人，这在这个州很重要。

sentences.en: Let's talk about the new GOP plan.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈新的共和党计划。

sentences.en: What would this new Republican plan ultimately mean for the patients who come to your clinic?
sentences.zh: 这个新的共和党计划最终对来到你们诊所的病人意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's probably for the working poor and those individual Medicaid.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这大概是针对穷苦工薪阶层和那些拥有个人医疗白卡的人。

sentences.en: It appears that there's going to be a significant reduction in services.
sentences.zh: 看来服务将会大幅缩减。

sentences.en: And by 2020, there may be, if that occurs, it might be as many as ours.
sentences.zh: 到 2020 年，如果这种情况发生，可能会有多达我们这样数量的人受影响。

sentences.en: That's a really big number.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常大的数字。

sentences.en: It's a huge number.
sentences.zh: 这是一个庞大的数字。

sentences.en: And what would that do to the community?
sentences.zh: 那会对社区造成什么影响？

sentences.en: We would continue to provide primary care as long as we were questioned that if the Republican, 25% of our patients, a number of those will.
sentences.zh: 只要我们被质询，如果我们继续提供初级保健，如果共和党计划导致我们 25% 的病人受到影响，其中的许多人将会……

sentences.en: Multiple chronic will continue to see me, but we won't be able to get health care.
sentences.zh: 患有多种慢性病的人会继续来看我，但我们将无法获得医疗保健。

sentences.en: I think the lack of affordable health care to the population I care for with the chronic disease they have will be devastating.
sentences.zh: 我认为，对于我所照顾的患有慢性病的群体来说，缺乏负担得起的医疗保健将是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: Well, doctor, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好吧，医生，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: I really appreciate you spending some time with us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你花时间接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: You take care.
sentences.zh: 保重。

sentences.en: You take care, and good luck with your community and your practice.
sentences.zh: 保重，祝你的社区和诊所一切顺利。

sentences.en: Well, we will continue to take care of patients regardless of their ability to pay to the best of our ability, and we'll go on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们将继续竭尽所能为患者提供医疗服务，不论他们的支付能力如何，我们将继续前行。

sentences.en: The key thing that a lot of people want to know, when I do my listening sessions, when I talk to people with various disease advocacy groups,
sentences.zh: 人们最想知道的关键事情是，当我举行听证会时，当我与各种疾病倡导团体的人交谈时，

sentences.en: is they just want to know that when we pass this, the next day they're not going to lose their health insurance.
sentences.zh: 是他们只想知道，当我们通过这项法律后，第二天他们不会失去医疗保险。

sentences.en: That's not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 这不会发生。

sentences.en: We pass this law, and the day after, Americans who have insurance aren't going to lose it the day after.
sentences.zh: 我们通过这项法律，而在第二天，拥有保险的美国人不会在第二天就失去保险。

sentences.en: We need to have a stable transition to conservative health care reform, and that's what we're doing,
sentences.zh: 我们需要向保守派医疗改革进行平稳过渡，这正是我们正在做的事情，

sentences.en: so that we do not pull the rug out from anybody who is enjoying some kind of coverage they have today.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就不会抽走任何今天正在享受某种保障的人脚下的地毯。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在黑胶时代的夜总会当DJ的时候，你每天晚上也是带着30万件最珍爱的藏品去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个像这样充满生机的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了精美的50年历史的老物件。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Dana.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫达娜。

sentences.en: I am a subscriber to The New York Times, but my husband isn't.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的订阅用户，但我丈夫不是。

sentences.en: And it would be really nice to be able to share a recipe or an article or compete with him in Wordle or Connections.
sentences.zh: 如果能和他分享食谱或文章，或者在Wordle和Connections字谜游戏里一决高下，那就太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Dana, we heard you.
sentences.zh: 达娜，我们听到了你的心声。

sentences.en: It's why we created the New York Times Family Subscription.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们推出《纽约时报》家庭订阅服务的原因。

sentences.en: One subscription, up to four separate logins for anyone in your life.
sentences.zh: 一份订阅，最多可为生活中的任何人提供四个独立的登录账号。

sentences.en: Find out more at nytimes.com slash family.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/family 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: Music has a way of reflecting the moment we're living in, as it happens, in a way that movies or TV, because they can take months and years to come together, can't.
sentences.zh: 音乐有一种方式，能即时反映我们生活的时代，而电影或电视因为需要数月甚至数年来制作，所以做不到这一点。

sentences.en: And so, The New York Times is partnering with writers and thinkers to collect songs from this past year that tell us something about this moment.
sentences.zh: 因此，《纽约时报》正与作家和思想家合作，收集过去一年里那些向我们诉说这个时代的歌曲。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to play you just three of those songs.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将为您播放其中三首歌。

sentences.en: First up, Solange.
sentences.zh: 首先是索兰热。

sentences.en: Novelist Angela Flournoy talks to Nisu Ababa, an editor at the magazine, about the song FUBU.
sentences.zh: 小说家安吉拉·弗卢尔诺伊与杂志编辑尼苏·阿巴巴就歌曲《FUBU》展开了讨论。

sentences.en: A warning, the song contains a word many find offensive.
sentences.zh: 温馨提示，这首歌包含了一个许多人觉得被冒犯的词。

sentences.en: So, I guess you should, I guess I'll let you describe, like, the conceit of FUBU.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想你应该……我想我还是让你来描述一下《FUBU》的创作构思吧。

sentences.en: Like, what's going on in the song and lyrics?
sentences.zh: 这首歌和歌词里到底在讲什么？

sentences.en: On the lyrical front, it's interesting, because the thing that's happening is, one, there's a clearly very important to her that people know who the song is for.
sentences.zh: 就歌词而言，这很有趣，因为发生的事情是，首先，对她来说，让大家知道这首歌是写给谁的，显然非常重要。

sentences.en: The first phrase is, one for us.
sentences.zh: 第一句歌词是，献给我们的一首歌。

sentences.en: It's for us and it's by us.
sentences.zh: 这是为我们而作，也由我们创作。

sentences.en: All my niggas in the whole wide world
sentences.zh: 我全世界所有的黑人兄弟们

sentences.en: When you first hear her say, um, can I say the word?
sentences.zh: 当你第一次听到她说，嗯，我可以讲这个词吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I was going to interrupt, but yeah, we can say whatever.
sentences.zh: 对，我本想打断，不过没关系，我们什么都可以说。

sentences.en: Right, so when you first hear her say,
sentences.zh: 没错，所以当你第一次听到她说，

sentences.en: All my niggas in the whole wide world
sentences.zh: 我全世界所有的黑人兄弟们

sentences.en: You're like, oh, Solange, now I don't want to go to the show, because it's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 你会想，哦，索兰热，我可不想去看她的演出，因为接下来就要发生那种事了。

sentences.en: The weird moment of watching other people really excitedly say the word, right?
sentences.zh: 看着别人兴高采烈地跟着说这个词，那种感觉很诡异，对吧？

sentences.en: What's actually going on in the lyrics?
sentences.zh: 歌词里到底在发生什么？

sentences.en: So the song lists small moments of just, like, kind of racial insult that it can happen in your day as a non-white person.
sentences.zh: 所以这首歌列举了作为非白人，你在日常生活中可能遇到的那种微小的人种侮辱时刻。

sentences.en: When a nigga trying to board the plane
sentences.zh: 当黑人试图登机时

sentences.en: You're trying to board the plane And they ask you your name again And they ask you your name again
sentences.zh: 你正努力登机 而他们又问你的名字 而他们又问你的名字

sentences.en: Those are the moments, for some reason, it's really fascinating that, um, in my experience, people who are not black take the most offense to when you try to tell them about.
sentences.zh: 不知为什么，这些时刻真的很吸引人，以我的经验来看，那些不是黑人的人，往往最反感你试图向他们倾诉这些。

sentences.en: Like, for instance, I lived in D.C., like a fancy high-rise, and it would happen all the time that people would ask me when I got in the elevator,
sentences.zh: 比如，我住在华盛顿特区一栋高级高层公寓里，每当我走进电梯，总会遇到这种事：

sentences.en: Do you know what floor you're going to?
sentences.zh: 你知道你要去几楼吗？

sentences.en: You know, not what floor are you going to, but do you know what floor you're going to?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，不是问你要去几楼，而是问你知道你要去几楼吗？

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: That's just one more way of making her black audience feel seen and feel kind of, like, this is an intimate space where, yes, I'm acknowledging that you are not crazy.
sentences.zh: 这只是又一种方式，让她的黑人听众感到被看见，并产生一种共鸣：是的，我承认你并没有疯。

sentences.en: She uses the N-word over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 她一遍又一遍地重复使用那个N开头的词。

sentences.en: But then later, she says, it's not for you to say, basically, in the song, you know, she says, You know, don't be mad, you can't say this word.
sentences.zh: 但后来她说，这不该由你来说，基本上在这首歌里，你知道，她说，别生气，你不能说这个词。

sentences.en: Be happy you have the whole world.
sentences.zh: 庆幸你拥有整个世界吧。

sentences.en: Which is sort of a little bit of an admonition to her non-black listeners, like,
sentences.zh: 这可以说是对她非白人听众的一点小小的警告，就像是，

sentences.en: I am telling you, you do not have permission to say this word, even if you enjoy this song.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你们，你们没有权限说这个词，即使你们很喜欢这首歌。

sentences.en: Next, writer Alexander Chee on Rufus Wainwright's A Woman's Face.
sentences.zh: 接下来，作家亚历山大·奇谈论鲁弗斯·温莱特的《女人的脸》。

sentences.en: He talks with Jake Silverstein, the editor of the magazine.
sentences.zh: 他与杂志主编杰克·西尔弗斯坦进行了交谈。

sentences.en: I have been a Rufus Wainwright fan since the beginning, but I didn't really think about him or his music until this last year when I bought a 2009 Subaru with my husband,
sentences.zh: 我从一开始就是鲁弗斯·温莱特的粉丝，但直到去年我和丈夫买了一辆2009年的斯巴鲁之前，我并没有真正去想过他或他的音乐，

sentences.en: and we discovered that it only had a 5-CD CD changer.
sentences.zh: 我们发现它只有一个只能放5张CD的换碟机。

sentences.en: And so, it was a revelation to load the CDs up in the car and go driving.
sentences.zh: 所以，把CD装进车里去兜风简直成了一种启示。

sentences.en: Around the same period, I went into a kind of, you know, what my doctor called a low-level depression.
sentences.zh: 差不多在同一时期，我陷入了一种，你知道的，我医生称之为轻度抑郁的状态。

sentences.en: Which, you know, if that's the low-level one, I'm terrified of what the severe one would be.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果这就是轻度的，那我简直不敢想象重度会是什么样。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, what I discovered in the process of driving around with my music again
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，我在重新开车听音乐的过程中发现，

sentences.en: was that there's this way that your favorite songs are a way of talking to you about yourself.
sentences.zh: 你最喜欢的歌曲其实是在以某种方式对你自己诉说。

sentences.en: Particularly in the car, maybe, when you're in this cocoon.
sentences.zh: 也许特别是在车里，当你身处这个小空间的时候。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think it might be a really American kind of communion with the self to drive and listen to music.
sentences.zh: 我想，开车听音乐可能是一种非常美国式的与自我交流的方式。

sentences.en: The song from the album that you selected to write about is based on Shakespeare's Sonnet No.
sentences.zh: 你选来撰文的专辑中的这首歌改编自莎士比亚的第20首十四行诗，

sentences.en: 20, and the song title on Wainwright's album is A Woman's Face.
sentences.zh: 而在温莱特的专辑中，这首歌的歌词标题是《女人的脸》。

sentences.en: What was it about this song that drew you to it?
sentences.zh: 是什么吸引你关注这首歌的？

sentences.en: First listening, I really just enjoyed the Torch Song quality of it.
sentences.zh: 初听时，我真的很喜欢它那种炽热情歌的特质。

sentences.en: And then I thought, uh, read the poem.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，呃，去读读这首诗吧。

sentences.en: Go find out what the poem is actually doing.
sentences.zh: 去看看这首诗究竟在表达什么。

sentences.en: And when I looked it up, I started laughing because I knew instantly the poem that it was.
sentences.zh: 当我查阅时，我忍不住笑了起来，因为我一眼就认出那是哪首诗了。

sentences.en: One of the clearest signs that Shakespeare might have been queer.
sentences.zh: 这是莎士比亚可能是酷儿的最清晰的迹象之一。

sentences.en: He's addressing a beautiful young man and saying, you're as beautiful as a woman, better than a woman, except for this one, this one thing.
sentences.zh: 他在赞美一个美丽的年轻男子，说你和一个女人一样美丽，甚至比女人更好，除了这一点，唯独这一点。

sentences.en: It's this situation that I know intimately from, especially from my college years,
sentences.zh: 这种情境我非常熟悉，尤其是在我的大学时代，

sentences.en: where I would have a friend who thought of himself as straight, having feelings he didn't understand, and, you know, saying to me things like, I wish you were a girl.
sentences.zh: 当时我有一个自认为是直男的朋友，他有了自己无法理解的情感，你知道的，他会对我说这样的话：我希望你是个女孩。

sentences.en: If you were a girl, everything would be perfect.
sentences.zh: 如果你是个女孩，一切就都完美了。

sentences.en: You know, him as a gay man singing about his life,
sentences.zh: 你知道，他作为一个同性恋男子歌唱自己的生活，

sentences.en: following his journey through these albums, helped me make one of my own.
sentences.zh: 跟随他这些专辑中的心路历程，帮助我开启了自己的心路历程。

sentences.en: And finally, Wesley Morris, the Times Culture Critic, on Adele's Send My Love to Your New Lover.
sentences.zh: 最后，时报文化评论人韦斯利·莫里斯谈论阿黛尔的《把我的爱留给你的新恋人》。

sentences.en: It's kind of an obnoxious song if you really think about it, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，这其实是一首有点讨人嫌的歌，对吧？

sentences.en: She's in this relationship.
sentences.zh: 她正处于这段关系中。

sentences.en: She's not getting what she wants out of it.
sentences.zh: 她没有从中得到她想要的东西。

sentences.en: But not only is she breaking up with him, she's making it seem like he's breaking up with her.
sentences.zh: 但她不仅要甩了他，还要搞得像是他在甩她一样。

sentences.en: He's not.
sentences.zh: 其实并没有。

sentences.en: He's just sitting there and she's doing everything.
sentences.zh: 他只是坐在那里，而一切都是她在主导。

sentences.en: She's so amazing.
sentences.zh: 她太厉害了。

sentences.en: Like, simultaneously self-empowered and self-pitying.
sentences.zh: 就像是既自我赋权又顾影自怜。

sentences.en: You know what it actually is, that self-pity, self-empowerment thing?
sentences.zh: 你知道那种自怜和自我赋权的结合究竟是什么吗？

sentences.en: It's the layering of the voices, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实是声音的交叠。

sentences.en: It's that she's got, like, her girls are with her, but her girls are herself.
sentences.zh: 也就是她虽然有闺蜜陪着，但她的闺蜜其实就是她自己。

sentences.en: And she's got backup for making this obnoxious decision.
sentences.zh: 她做出了这个讨人嫌的决定，背后有自己的支持。

sentences.en: This obnoxious self-empowerment decision.
sentences.zh: 这个讨人嫌的自我赋权决定。

sentences.en: It's that.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: What You Just Heard is part of a collaboration with The New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚听到的节目是与《纽约时报杂志》合作项目的一部分。

sentences.en: Their second annual music issue comes out this weekend.
sentences.zh: 他们的第二届年度音乐特刊将于本周末出版。

sentences.en: You can find it at nytimes.com slash 25 songs.
sentences.zh: 你可以访问 nytimes.com/25songs 了解详情。

sentences.en: To hear more interviews about the year's most meaningful songs, you can subscribe to the EP version on iTunes.
sentences.zh: 要想收听更多关于今年最有意义的歌曲的采访，你可以在iTunes上订阅EP版本的节目。

sentences.en: Search for The EP.
sentences.zh: 搜索“The EP”。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: After exposing secret CIA techniques for breaking into smartphones and TVs, the founder of WikiLeaks, Julian Assange, now says he will work with technology companies
sentences.zh: 在曝光了美国中情局入侵智能手机和小电视的秘密技术之后，维基解密创始人朱利安·阿桑奇现在表示，他将与科技公司合作

sentences.en: to strengthen the security of those products.
sentences.zh: 以加强这些产品的安全性。

sentences.en: And the head of the Environmental Protection Agency, Scott Pruitt, is publicly breaking with the scientific consensus inside his own agency on the causes of climate change.
sentences.zh: 美国环境保护局局长斯科特·普鲁特公开与该机构内部关于气候变化原因的科学共识分道扬镳。

sentences.en: Do you believe that it's been proven that CO2 is the primary control knob for climate?
sentences.zh: 你是否认为已经证明二氧化碳是气候变化的主要控制旋钮？

sentences.en: Do you believe that?
sentences.zh: 你相信这一点吗？

sentences.en: No, I think that measuring with precision human activity on the climate is something very challenging to do, and there's tremendous disagreement about the degree of impact.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为精确测量人类活动对气候的影响是一件非常具有挑战性的事情，而且对于影响程度存在着巨大的分歧。

sentences.en: So no, I would not agree that it's a primary contributor to the global warming that we see.
sentences.zh: 所以不，我不同意它是我们看到的全球变暖的主要推手。

sentences.en: As of Thursday night, the EPA website says,
sentences.zh: 截至周四晚上，环保局的网站上写道：

sentences.en: Quote, carbon dioxide is the primary greenhouse gas that is contributing to recent climate change.
sentences.zh: “引用，二氧化碳是导致近期气候变化的主要温室气体。”

sentences.en: The Daily is produced by Theo Balcom, Andy Mills, and Lisa Tobin.
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》由西奥·巴尔科姆、安迪·米尔斯和莉萨·托宾制作。

sentences.en: Samantha Hennig is our editorial director.
sentences.zh: 萨曼莎·亨尼格是我们的主编。

sentences.en: Pedro Rosado is our studio manager.
sentences.zh: 佩德罗·罗萨多是我们的录音室经理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks this week to Kelly Prime, Andrew Phelps,
sentences.zh: 本周特别感谢凯利·普赖姆、安德鲁·菲尔普斯、

sentences.en: Vanessa Romo, and Jeff Taylor.
sentences.zh: 瓦妮莎·罗莫和杰夫·泰勒。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 我们周一见。
